preamble: Under Grimm's law the Proto-Indo-European voiced aspirate *gʰ became Proto-Germanic /ɡ/~/ɣ/, realized as the fricative [ɣ] between vowels (and probably word-initially) and as [ɡ] after nasals and in gemination. The fricative survives in Dutch and Low German g. Outside Germanic the aspirate usually devoiced (Italic *x > h) or deaspirated (Balto-Slavic, Iranian g).

examples.note: Gothic steigan, Old English stīgan, Dutch stijgen with [ɣ].
Old Norse gestr, Old English ġiest.
Initial *gʰ shows the same Grimm's law outcome.

sources: Ringe, D. (2006). From Proto-Indo-European to Proto-Germanic. Oxford University Press.
